translations.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was in the beginning with God.
All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made that was made.
Through him was life, and that life was the light of men.
And that light shines in the darkness, and the darkness could not overtake it.
And there was a man sent from God, and his name was John.
He came for witness, to bear witness about that light, so that all might believe through him.
He was not that light, but came to bear witness about that light.
[?But] that was the true light, which enlightens every person coming into the world.
He was in this world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him.
He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.
But to those who received him he gave the power to become children of God, to those who believed in his name,
who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we saw his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
John bears witness about him; he cried out and said: "This was the one of whom I said: He who comes after me was before me, for he was before me."
For from his fullness we have all received grace in place of grace,
for the law was given by the hand of Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God; but the only-begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known.
And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites to him from Jerusalem to ask him: "Who are you?"
And he confessed and did not deny; he confessed: "I am not the Christ."
And they asked him: "Then who are you? Are you Elijah?" And he said to them: "No." "Are you the Prophet?" He answered: "No."
"Then tell us who you are, so that we may report to those who sent us. What shall we say about you?"
"I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness: Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said."
And those who had been sent were from among the Pharisees.
They asked him and said to him: "Then why do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"
John answered them and said: "I baptize you with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know,
the one who is to come after me, whose sandal straps I am not worthy to untie."
This took place at Bethabara, beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
On the next day he saw Jesus coming toward him, and he said: "Behold, here is the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world."
"This is the one of whom I told you: 'After me comes a man who was before me, because he was before me.'
"And I did not know him; but so that he might be revealed to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing with water."
John testified and said: "I saw the Spirit coming down from heaven like a dove, and it remained upon him.

"And I did not know him; but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me: 'The one on whom you see the Spirit coming down and remaining upon him, he is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'
"And I have seen and testified that this is the Son of God."
On the next day John was standing there, with two of his disciples.
And he saw Jesus coming, and he said: "Behold, here is the Christ, the Lamb of God."
The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following him. He said to them: "What are you looking for?" They said to him: "Rabbi" (which is translated "Teacher"), "where is your dwelling?"
He said to them: "Come and see." They came and saw where his dwelling was, and they stayed with him that day, for it was about the tenth hour.
Andrew, Peter's brother, was one of the two who had heard John and followed him.
He first found his own brother Simon and said to him: "We have found the Messiah" (which is translated "Christ").
He brought them to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said: "Are you Simon, son of Jonah? You shall be called Cephas" (which is translated "Rock").
On the next day, as he was about to go out to Galilee, he found Philip, and Jesus said to him: "Follow me."
And Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him: "We have found the one of whom Moses wrote in the Law, and the prophets: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth."
Nathanael said to him: "Can anything good come from Nazareth?" Philip said to him: "Come and see."
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said of him: "Behold, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit."
Nathanael said to him: "How do you know me?" Jesus answered and said to him: "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."
Nathanael answered and said: "Rabbi, are you the Son of God? Are you the King of Israel?"
Jesus answered him and said: "Because I told you, 'I saw you under the fig tree,' you believe? You will see greater things than this."
And he said to him: "Truly, truly I say to you: you will see the heavens opened and the angels of God going up and coming down upon the Son of Man."
And on the third day there was a wedding at Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
Jesus and his disciples too were invited to that wedding.
And when the wine ran short, his mother said to Jesus: "They have no wine."
Jesus said to her: "What is there between you and me, woman? My hour has not yet come."
His mother said to the servants: "Whatever he tells you, do it."
Six marble jars stood there, for the purification of the Jews; each of them held two or three measures.
Jesus said to them: "Fill those jars with water!" And they filled them.
And he said to them: "Draw some out and take it to the master of the feast and the head of this house!" And they took it to him.
And when the head of the house tasted the water that had been turned into wine, and did not know where it came from (though the servants knew), the head of the house answered the bridegroom
and said: "Every man serves the good wine first, and when they have become drunk, then the inferior [?] as well. You have kept the good wine until now."
Jesus did this, the beginning of his signs, at Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this Jesus went down to Capernaum, he himself and his mother and his brothers, and he stayed there not many days.
And the feast of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
And in the temple he found people selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the money-changers sitting there.
And he made a whip of rope and drove them all out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen; and he scattered the copper coins of the dealers [?] and overturned their tables.
And to those who were selling doves he said: "Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
Then his disciples remembered that it is written: "Zeal for your house will consume me."
The Jews answered and said to him: "What sign will you show us, since you are doing this?"
Jesus answered and said: "Destroy this temple, and on the third day I will raise it up."
The Jews said to him: "This temple was built in forty-six years, and you will raise it up in three days?"
But he was speaking of his own body as the temple.
And when he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that this was what he had been saying, and they believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
And while he was in Jerusalem at the feast, many believed in his name, because they saw the signs that he was doing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them at all, because he himself knew, for all [?] knew him.
And he had no need for anyone to testify to him about man, for he himself knew what was in man.
And there was a man from among the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
He came to him by night and said to him, "Rabbi, we know that you have been sent from God as a teacher, for no one can do such signs as you do unless God is with him."
Jesus answered and said to him, "Truly, truly, I tell you: unless someone is born from above, he cannot enter the kingdom of God."
Nicodemus said to him, "How can an old man be born from above? Can he enter his mother's womb a second time and be born?"
Jesus answered and said, "Truly, truly, I tell you: unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
For what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be amazed that I told you that you must be born from above.
For the wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit."
Nicodemus answered and said to him, "How can this be?"
Jesus answered and said, "You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know this?
Truly, truly, I tell you: we speak what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, yet you do not accept our testimony.
Now I have told you only these earthly things, and you do not believe; how then will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
And no one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes in him may receive eternal life.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son for it, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but receive eternal life.
For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
Whoever believes in him is not judged, and whoever does not believe in him is already judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
And this is the judgment: that the light has come into the world, and people loved darkness more than light, because their deeds were evil.
For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed.
But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be made plain, that they have been done through God."
After this Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and there he stayed with the disciples and baptized.
John was also there, at Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there, and people came and were baptized.
For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
Now there arose a discussion between the disciples of John and the Jews about purification.
They came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you bore witness: look, he is baptizing, and everyone is going to him."
John answered and said, "A man cannot receive anything by himself unless it has been given to him from heaven above.
You yourselves are my witnesses that I told you, 'I am not the Christ, but I have been sent before him.'

For he who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and listens to him, rejoices greatly at the voice of the bridegroom. Now this joy, which is mine, has been fulfilled.
He must increase, and I must decrease.
He who comes from above is over [?] all. He who is of this earth is from the earth and speaks of the earth. He who comes down from heaven
testifies to what he has seen and heard, and no one accepts his testimony.
Whoever accepts his testimony has set his seal to this, that God is true.
For he whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God did not give the Spirit by measure.
The Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son will receive eternal life, and whoever does not believe in the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God will remain upon him."
When the Lord learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John
(although Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples),
he left the land of Judea and went back again to Galilee.
And he had to pass through Samaria.
He came to a city of the Samaritans called Sychar, near the field that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
Jacob's well was there, and Jesus, wearied from the journey, sat by the well. It was about the sixth hour.
A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Give me a drink."
For his disciples had gone into the city to buy food.
The Samaritan woman said to him, "You are a Jew; how is it that you ask a drink of me, a Samaritan woman?" For Jews never associate with Samaritans.
Jesus answered and said to her, "If you had known the gift of God, and who it is that is saying to you, 'Give me a drink,' you would have asked him, and he would [?] have given you living water."
The woman said to him, "Lord, you have no bucket, and this well is deep. Where then do you get living water?
Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well? He himself drank from it, and his sons and his flocks."
Jesus answered and said to her, "Everyone who drinks of that water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again. The water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water welling up to eternal life.
The woman said to him: "Lord, give me that water, so that I will not be thirsty and will not have to come here to draw water."
Jesus said to her: "Go, call your husband, and come here."
The woman answered and said: "I have no husband." Jesus said to her: "You were right to say, 'I have no husband,'
for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband. What you said is true."
The woman said to him: "Lord, I think that you are a prophet.
Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that only in Jerusalem is the place where it is right to worship."
Jesus said to her: "Woman, believe me, the hours are coming when they will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.
But the hours are coming, and are already here, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father is seeking such worshippers.
God is spirit, and his worshippers must worship in spirit and in truth."

The woman said: "I know that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything." Jesus said to her: "I am he, the one who is speaking to you." At this word his disciples arrived, and they were amazed that he was speaking with a woman. But none of them said, "What are you looking for?" or "Why are you speaking with her?"
The woman left her water jar, went into the city, and said to the people:
"Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Could he be the Christ?"
They went out of the city and came toward him.
Meanwhile, before they had reached him, his disciples were urging him, saying: "Teacher, eat some bread!"
He said to them: "I have food to eat that you do not know about."
The disciples said to one another: "Has someone brought him something to eat?"
Jesus said to them: "My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his works.
Do you not say, 'Four months more, and the harvest will come'? Look, I tell you: lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they have turned white and are ready for harvest.
Whoever reaps receives a reward and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
In this the saying holds true: one sows and another reaps.
I am sending you to reap what you did not work for. Others have worked, and you have entered into their labour."
Many Samaritans from that city believed in him because of the word of the woman who testified: "He told me everything I have done."
When the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them, and he stayed there two days.
And many more believed in him because of his words.
And they said to the woman: "We no longer believe because of what you said, for we have heard him ourselves, and we know that this is truly the Saviour of the world."
And after two days he went on from there and departed for Galilee.
For he himself had testified that a prophet is without honour in his own country.
But when he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, for they had also seen the many signs he had done in Jerusalem at the feast, since they too had gone to the feast.
Then he came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. And there was a certain royal official there whose own son lay sick in Capernaum.
When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he came to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, for he was near death.
Jesus said to him: "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe."
The royal official said to him: "Lord, come down before my child dies."
Jesus said to him: "Go; your son is alive." And the man believed the word that he had spoken to him, and he went away.

And as he was going down, his servants met him joyfully and said: "Your child is alive." He asked them about the hour: "At what hour did he get better?" They said to him: "Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him."
The father remembered that this was the hour at which Jesus had said to him: "Your son is alive." And he himself believed, along with his whole household.
This was the second sign that Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.
After this there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
And in Jerusalem, at the sheep pool, there was a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew, which had five porticoes.
In these lay a great crowd of sick people: the blind, the withered and the lame, waiting for the water to be stirred.
And there was a man there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had already been there a long time, he said to him: "Do you want to be made well?"
The sick man said to him: "Lord, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am dragging myself along, someone else goes down ahead of me."
Jesus said to him: "Get up, pick up your bed and go!"
And the man was healed. He got up, picked up his bed and walked. And that day was the Sabbath.
The Jews said to the man who had been healed: "It is the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to carry that bed."
He answered them: "The man who healed me said to me: 'Pick up your bed and go.'"
They asked him: "Who is the man who said to you, 'Pick up your bed and walk'?"
But the man who had been healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away from the crowd in that place.
After this Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: "Look, you have been healed. Do not sin any more, so that nothing worse happens to you."
The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
And for this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he was doing this on the Sabbath.
Jesus answered them: "My Father is working until now, and I am working too."
For this reason the Jews sought all the more to kill him, not only because he was breaking the Sabbath, but because he claimed God as his own Father and made himself equal to God.
Jesus answered and said to them: "Truly, truly I say to you: the Son of Man cannot do anything by himself, unless he sees what the Father is doing; for whatever he does, the Son also does likewise.
For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself does, and he will show him works greater than these, so that you may marvel.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wishes.
And the Father does not judge anyone, but has given all judgment to the Son,
so that all may honour the Son just as they honour the Father. Whoever glorifies the Son also glorifies the Father, who sent him.
Truly, truly I say to you that whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me will receive eternal life and will not come into judgment, but will pass from death to life.
Truly, truly I say to you that the hour is coming, and is already here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God; and those who hear will live.
For just as the Father has life in himself, so he has also granted the Son to have life in himself.
And he has given him authority to judge, and because he is the Son of Man.
Why do you marvel at this? For the hour will come in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice.
And they will come out [?] ... [?] testimony; but I say this so that you may be saved.
He was a lamp that was kindled and shining, and for a time you were willing to rejoice in his light.
But I have testimony greater than John's: the works that the Father gave me to accomplish [?], these same works that I do testify about me that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me, he testifies about me. You have never heard his voice, nor have you seen his flash of light [?].
Nor do his words dwell among you, for you do not believe the one whom he sent.
Search the Scriptures, for you think that through them you will obtain eternal life; and they are the ones that testify about me, through which you think, concerning me [?], to obtain life.
And you do not want to come to me, so that [?]
I do not accept glory from people.
But I know you, that you do not have the love of God.
I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not accept me. If someone else comes in his own name, him you will accept.
How can you come to believe, when you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
Do not think that I have spoken against you before God. There is one who accuses you: Moses, in whom you place your hope.
If you had believed Moses, you would have believed me too, for he wrote about me.
If you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe these words of mine?
After this Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee, toward the region of Tiberias.
And a great crowd followed him, because they saw the signs that he was performing on the sick.
Jesus went up the mountain and sat down there with his disciples.
And the feast of the Jews was near.
Jesus raised his eyes and saw the great crowd that was coming to him. He said to Philip, "Where shall we buy bread so that they may eat?"
He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered him, "Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, even if each of them took only a little."
One of the disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him:
"There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish. But what use are these among so many?"
Jesus said, "Make these men sit down." There was a great deal of grass in that place, and the men sat down, about five thousand in number.
Then Jesus took the bread, gave thanks, and distributed it to those who were seated, and likewise of the fish, as much as they wanted.
When they had eaten their fill, he said to his disciples, "Gather up the leftover fragments, so that nothing is lost."
So they gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with the fragments of the five barley loaves that were left over by those who had eaten.
When the men saw the sign that he had performed, they said, "This is truly the prophet who was to come into the world."
When Jesus realized that they were about to seize him and make him king, he withdrew again to the mountain by himself alone.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the seashore
and got into a boat and set out across the sea toward Capernaum. It had already grown dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them,
and the sea was getting rough because of strong winds.
When they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near the boat, and they were terrified.
But he said to them, "It is I; do not be afraid!"
And they wanted him to come up into the boat. And at once the boat reached the land they were heading for.

On the next day the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea saw that there was no other boat there, only one, the one the disciples of Jesus had been in. For Jesus had not gone into that boat with his disciples; only his disciples had gone away.
Other boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread.
And when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, and neither were his disciples, they turned the boat around and came to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
And when they found him on the other side of the sea, they said to him: "Rabbi, when did you come here?"
Jesus answered them and said: "Truly, truly I say to you: you are looking for me not because you saw a sign, but because you ate of the bread and were filled.
Go, do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that remains for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you, for God the Father has set his seal on him."
They said to him: "What shall we do in order to do the works of God?"
Jesus answered them and said: "These are the works of God: that you believe in the one who sent me."
They said to him: "What sign do you do, so that we may see it and believe you? What have you done?
The fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat."
Jesus said to them: "Truly, truly I say to you: it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven; rather, my Father will give you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread is from God, which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world."
They said: "Lord, give us that bread at all times."
And Jesus said to them: "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst.
But as I told you: you have seen me and you do not believe.
Everyone whom the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will not drive out.
For I have come down from heaven not to do my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
This is the will of the one who sent me: that of all whom the Father has given me I should lose none, but should raise him up on the last day.
This is the will of my Father: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should receive eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day."
The Jews murmured about him because he said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven,"
and they said: "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose mother and father we know? How then does he now say, 'I have come down from heaven'?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "Why are you murmuring among yourselves?
No one is able to come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: 'And they shall all be taught by God.' Everyone who hears from the Father and learns will come to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.
Truly, truly I say to you: whoever believes will receive eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness and died.
This is the bread that came down from heaven, so that whoever eats of it will not die.
I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
The Jews argued with one another and said: How can this man give us his flesh to eat?
Jesus said to them: Truly, truly I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you will not have life in yourselves.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood will have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For my flesh is true food, and my blood is true drink.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood will dwell with me, and I with him.
As the living Father sent me, I too live with the Father; and whoever eats my flesh will live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven, not like the manna your fathers ate and died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.
He said this to the people while teaching in Capernaum.
When many of his disciples heard this, they spoke up and said: This saying is hard. Who can bear to listen to it?
When Jesus knew in himself that his disciples were grumbling about this, he said to them: Does this make you stumble?
What, then, if you were to see the Son of Man going up to where he was before?
It is the Spirit that gives life; the flesh is of no use at all. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and they are life.
For Jesus knew from the beginning who the ones were who did not believe, and who it was who would betray him.
And he said: This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been granted to him by my Father.
Because of this many of his disciples turned back and no longer went about with him.
Jesus said to the twelve disciples: Do you also perhaps want to go away?
Simon Peter answered him and said: Lord, where would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Christ, the Son of God.
Jesus answered them: Did I not choose you, the twelve? Yet one of you is a devil.
He was speaking of Judas son of Simon Iscariot, for he was going to betray him, and he was one of the twelve.
And the Jewish feast of Tabernacles was near.
His brothers said to him: "Leave here and go to Judea, so that the disciples may see the works you are doing.
For no one does anything in secret and at the same time shows himself boldly. If you are doing these things, show yourself to the world."
For even his brothers did not believe in him.
Jesus said to them: "My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I expose it, for its works are evil.
You go up. I will not go up to this feast, for my time has not yet been fulfilled."
Having said this, he himself stayed there in Galilee.
When his brothers had gone up, then he himself also went up to the feast, not openly but in secret.
And the Jews were looking for him at the feast and saying: "Where is he?"
And there was murmuring among the people about him. Some said: "He is good." Others said: "No, he leads this people astray."
And no one spoke openly about him, out of fear of the Jews.
Only when the feast was half over did Jesus go up into the temple, and he was teaching.
And the Jews were amazed and said: "How does this man know the Scriptures, when he has not studied?"
Jesus answered them and said: "This teaching of mine is not mine, but belongs to the one who sent me.
If anyone wishes to do his will, he will understand about this teaching, whether it is from God or whether I speak on my own.
Whoever speaks on his own seeks his own glory. But whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no deceit in him.
Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why are you seeking to kill me?"
The people answered and said: "You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill you?"
Jesus answered and said to them: "I did one deed, and you are amazed at it.
Moses gave you circumcision (not that it came from Moses, but from the fathers), and on the Sabbath day you circumcise a man.
If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath day so that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because I made a man entirely well on the Sabbath?
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment."
Some of the people of Jerusalem said: "Is this not the man they were seeking to kill?
Look, here he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers really know that this is the Christ?"
But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.
Jesus cried out in the temple as he taught, and said: "You know me, and you know where I am from. I have not come of my own accord; but the one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.
I know him, because I am from him, and he sent me."
They wanted to seize him, but he got out of their hands, and no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.
Many of the people believed in him, and they said: "When the Christ comes, will he do any greater sign than this man does?"
The Pharisees heard the people murmuring about him. The chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize him.
Jesus said to them: "I am with you a little while longer, and then I am going to the one who sent me.
You will seek me and you will not find me; and where I am, you cannot come."
The Jews said to one another: "Where is he going to go, that we will not find him? Will he go to the Gentiles who are scattered abroad and teach the Gentiles?
What is this saying that he said: 'You will seek me and you will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come'?"
On the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying: "If anyone thirsts, let him come to me — [?]
Whoever believes in me, as the scripture says, rivers of living water will flow out of his belly."
He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were to receive; for the Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
When some of the people heard these words, they said: "This is truly the prophet."
Others said: "This is the Christ." But some said: "Surely the Christ is not to come from Galilee?
Does not the scripture say that the Christ is to come from the seed of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?"
So there was a division among the people because of him.
Some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid a hand on him.
Then the officers of the priests and the Pharisees came back, and these said to them: "Why did you not bring him?"
The officers answered and said: "No man has ever spoken the way that man speaks."
The Pharisees answered and said to them: "Have you also been led astray?
Has any of the rulers or any of the Pharisees believed in him?
But this confused mob, who do not know the law, are accursed."
Nicodemus, who had come to him by night before, and who was one of them, said to them:
"Does our law judge a man without first hearing from him and learning what he is doing?"
They answered him and said to him, "Are you also a Galilean? Search and see, for no prophet will arise from Galilee."
The Pharisees said to him, "You testify about yourself, and your testimony is not true."
Jesus answered and said to them, "Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, for I know where I have come from and where I am going."
"You judge according to the flesh, but I judge no one."
"And if I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone, but it is I and the Father who sent me."
"And in your law too it is written that the testimony of two men is true."
"I am the one who testifies about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me."
They said to him, "Where is your Father?" Jesus answered and said to them, "You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, perhaps you would know my Father also."
He spoke these words in the treasury, while he was teaching in the temple. And no one seized him, for his hour had not yet come.
He said to them, "I am Jesus. I am going away, and you will seek me and will not find me, and you will die in your sins, for where I am going, you cannot come."
The Jews said, "Surely he will not kill himself, since he says, 'Where I am going, you cannot come'?"
And he said to them, "You are from below, and I am from above; you are of this world, I am not of this world."
"But I told you that you will die in your sins; if you do not believe me, that I am he, you will die in your sins."
They said to him, "Who are you?" Jesus said to them, "First of all, this: that I am also telling you."
"I have many words and judgments concerning you, but the Father who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, that I speak to this world."
And they did not understand that he was speaking to them about his Father.
Jesus said to them, "When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will understand that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, so I speak."
"And he who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him."
As he was saying this, many believed in him.
Jesus said to the Jews who had believed, "If you abide in my words, you will be my true disciples."
"And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
They answered him and said to him, "We are descendants of Abraham and have never been slaves to anyone; how can you say, 'You will become free'?"
Jesus answered, "Truly, truly I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin."
"And the slave does not remain in the house forever, but the son remains forever."
"If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free."
I know that you are descendants of Abraham, but you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place among you.
I speak what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have heard from your father.
They answered and said to him, "Our father is Abraham." Jesus answered and said, "If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.
But now you seek to kill me, a man who tells you the truth that I heard from my Father. Abraham did not do this.
You do the works of your father." They said to him, "We were not born of fornication; we have one Father: God."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love [?] me, for I came forth from God, and I did not come of my own accord, but he sent me.
Why do you not understand my words? Because you are unable to hear my words.

You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is [?] no truth in him. Whenever he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own, for he is a liar, and the father of it too.
But because I tell you the truth, you do not believe me.
Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell you the truth, why do you not believe me?
Whoever is of God hears the words of God; and the reason you do not hear is that you are not of God."
The Jews answered and said to him, "Did we not say rightly that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
Jesus answered and said, "I do not have a demon; rather, I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges.
Truly, truly, I say to you: if anyone keeps my words, he will never see death, forever."
The Jews said to him, "Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets too, and you say, 'If anyone hears my words, he will never taste death, forever.'
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets also perished. Who do you make yourself out to be?"
Jesus answered and said, "If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is the Father who glorifies me, of whom you say, 'He is our God.'
And you have not known him, but I know him. If I were to say, 'I do not know him,' I would be found a liar like you; but I know him and I keep his words.
Your father Abraham longed to see my day; he saw it and rejoiced."
The Jews said to him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?"
Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I say to you: before Abraham came to be, I was."
They took up stones to throw at him. Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple.
And as he was passing by, he saw a man who was blind from birth.
His disciples asked him and said, "Rabbi, whose sin is it, this man's or his parents', that he was born blind?"
Jesus answered: "It is not his sin, nor his parents', but it happened so that the works of God might be revealed in him.
We must do the works of the one who sent me while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
While I am in this world, I am the light of the world."
When he had said this, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle, and he smeared the clay on the eyes of the blind man,
and said to him: "Go and wash in the pool of Siloam" (which means "Sent"). He went and washed, and he came back, and he who had once been blind could see [?].
It was the Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened the blind man's eyes.
Then the Pharisees questioned him and said to him: "How do you see?" He said to them: "He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
Some of the Pharisees said: "That man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath." Others said: "How can a sinful man do such a sign?" And there was division among them.
Then they said to the blind man: "What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?" He said: "He is a prophet."
The Jews did not believe that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of the man who had received his sight.
They questioned them and said: "Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? How then does he see now?"
His parents answered and said: "We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind.
But how he now sees we do not know, and who opened his eyes we do not know. Ask him; he is of age; he will speak for himself."
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had agreed that if anyone confessed him to be the Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.
That is why his parents said: "He is of age; ask him."
Then for a second time they called the man who had once been blind and said to him: "Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner."
He said: "Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. But one thing I do know: I was blind, and now I see."
Then they said to him: "What did he do to you, and how did he open your eyes?"
He answered them: "Look, I have already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you also want to become his disciples?"
They reviled him and said: "You be his disciple! We are disciples of Moses.
We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he comes from."
The man answered and said to them: "This is the amazing thing: you do not know where he comes from, and yet he opened my eyes.
I know that God does not listen to sinners, but if someone worships God and does his will, God listens to him.
Never since the world began has anyone heard of someone opening the eyes of a man born blind.
If this man were not from God, he could do nothing."
They answered and said to him, "You were born entirely in sin, and are you teaching us?" And they drove him out.
Jesus heard that they had driven him out. And when he found him, he said to him, "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
He answered and said, "Lord, who is he, that I may believe in him?"
Jesus said to him, "You have seen him, and the one who is speaking to you is he."
And he said, "I believe, Lord," and he worshipped him.
And Jesus said, "I came into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this, and they said to him, "Are we also blind, then?"
Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would have no guilt; but now you say, 'We see,' and so your sin remains firmly upon you."
"Truly, truly, I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the door but climbs in some other way is a thief and a robber.
But whoever enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
The doorkeeper opens to him, and the sheep hear his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
And he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
But they will not follow a stranger; instead they flee from him, because they do not know the stranger's voice."
Jesus told them this parable, but they did not understand what it was that he was saying to them.
Then Jesus said to them again, "Truly, truly, I say to you: I am the door of the sheep.
All who came before me were thieves and robbers, and the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved; he will go in and go out and find pasture.
The thief comes for no other reason than to steal and to slaughter and to destroy. I came so that they may have life, and have it more abundantly.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.
But the hired man is not the shepherd, and the sheep are not his own. When he sees the wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches them and scatters them.
For he is employed for wages, and he does not care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd, and I know my own, and my own know me,
just as my Father knows me and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.
And I have other sheep that are not of this fold, and I must bring them here as well; and they will hear my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.
For this reason my Father loves me: because I lay down my life so that I may take it up again.
No one can take it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. This commandment I have received from my Father.
Then there was a division among the Jews because of these words.
And many of them were saying, "He has a demon and is raving. Why do you listen to him?"
Others were saying, "These are not the words of one possessed by a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?"
It was the feast of the Dedication in Jerusalem, and it was winter.
And Jesus was walking in the temple, in Solomon's portico.
The Jews surrounded him and said to him, "How long will you keep our souls in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered them and said, "I told you, and you did not believe me. The works that I do in the name of my Father, these bear witness about me.
But you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
And I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hands.
My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch them out of the hands of my Father.
I and my Father are one."
They took up stones in order to stone him.
Jesus answered them, "I have shown you many good works from my Father; for which kind of them are you stoning me?"
The Jews answered him, "We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, because you are a man and you make yourself out to be God."
Jesus answered them, "Is it not written in your law, 'I said, you are gods'?
If he called them gods to whom the word of God came, and the Scripture cannot be broken,
then do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, 'You are blaspheming,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe these works, so that you may know and understand that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father."
Then they sought to seize him, and he went out from their hands and departed again.
And he crossed the Jordan, to the place where John had first been baptizing, and he stayed there.
And many came to him and said, "John did no sign, but everything that John said about this man was true."
And many believed in him there.
And there was a certain man who was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, the village of Mary and of Martha her sister.
This was the Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair; it was her brother Lazarus who was sick.
His sisters sent to him and said to him: "Lord, behold, the one whom you love is sick."
When Jesus heard this, he said: "This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it."
And Jesus loved Mary and Martha her sister, and Lazarus.
When he heard that he was sick, he stayed two days in the place where he was.
Then, after this, he said to his disciples: "Come, let us go to Judea again."
The disciples said to him: "Teacher, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?"
Jesus answered: "Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the daytime, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
And if anyone walks at night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him."
After he had said this, he then said to them: "Lazarus, our friend, has fallen asleep, but I will go and wake him."
The disciples said to him: "If he is sleeping, he will recover."
But Jesus had spoken of his death, and they thought that he was speaking of the rest of sleep.
Then Jesus said to them plainly: "Lazarus has died.
And for your sake I rejoice that I was not there, so that you may believe. But now come, and let us go to him."
Thomas, who was called the Twin, said to his fellow disciples: "Let us go too, so that we may die with him."
Jesus came and found that he had been four days in the tomb.
And Bethany was near Jerusalem, only about fifteen stadia away.
Many of the Jews had come to Mary and Martha to comfort them concerning their brother.
When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him, but Mary stayed sitting in the house.
Martha said to Jesus: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you."
Jesus said to her: "Your brother will rise again."
Martha said to him: "I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day."
Jesus said to her: "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live."
And everyone who lives and believes in me shall not die forever. Do you believe this?
She said to him: Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.
And when she had said this, she went away and called Mary, her sister, secretly, and said to her: The Teacher is here and is calling you.
When she heard this, she rose quickly and went to him.
Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.

Now the Jews who were with her in the house and were comforting her, when they saw Mary rise up in great haste and go out, they also went out and followed her, supposing that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
And when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him: Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
When Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who were with her weeping, he was stirred in his spirit, like one angered,
and said: Where have you laid him? They said to him: Lord, come and see.
And Jesus wept.
And the Jews said: See how much he loved him!
Some of them said: Could not this man, who opened the eyes of that blind man, have made it so that this man also would not die?
Then Jesus, again angered in his mind, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
And Jesus said to them: Take away that stone. Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him: Lord, by now he stinks, for it is the fourth day.
Jesus said to her: Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?
And when they had taken away the stone, Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: Father, I thank you that you have heard me.
And I knew that you always hear me, but I say this for the sake of this people standing around, so that they may believe that you sent me.
When he had said this, he cried out with a loud voice and said: Lazarus, arise and come out!
And the dead man came out, bound foot and hand with strips of cloth, and his face was wrapped with a napkin. Jesus said to them: Unbind him and let him go.
And many of the Jews who had come to Mary, when they saw what he had done, believed in him.
But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
And the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered in [?] (council) and said: What shall we do, for this man performs many signs?
If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Greeks will come and wipe out our nation and this place.
One of them, whose name was Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them: You know nothing,
nor have you considered anything, that it is better for us that one man should die for this people, and that this whole nation should not perish.
He did not say this of his own accord. Because he was high priest that year, he spoke prophetically that Jesus was going to die for the nation.
And not only for this nation, but also so that the scattered children would be gathered together into one.
And from that day on they plotted how they might kill him.
So from then on Jesus no longer went about openly among the Jews. Instead he went from there to a region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and he stayed there with his disciples.
The Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves.
They were looking for Jesus, wanting to see him, and those standing in the temple said to one another, "What do you think? Will he not come to this feast?"
The chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, "Tell us," so that they might arrest him.
Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, the one who had died and whom he had raised from the dead.
There they prepared a supper for him. Martha served him, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him.
Then Mary took a pound of choice, very costly ointment of nard and anointed Jesus' feet, and she wiped his feet with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
One of the disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was about to betray him, said to him:
"Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?"
He said this not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. He had charge of the money box, and he kept what was put into it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of my burial clothing."
"You always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me."
A large crowd of the Jews learned that he was there, and they came, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests plotted to kill Lazarus as well.
Because of him many of the Jews were going over and believing.
The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
They took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, crying out, "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!"
Jesus found a donkey and sat on it, as it is written:
"Rejoice, daughter of Zion! Behold, your king is coming, seated on a donkey's colt."
His disciples did not understand these things at first. But when Jesus was glorified, they remembered that this had been written about him, and that they had done these things to him.
The crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept testifying.
This is why the crowd went to meet him: they had heard that he had done this sign.
But the Pharisees said to one another: "Do you see that you gain nothing? Look, the whole world has gone after him."
There were also some Gentiles there, who had gone up to worship at the feast.
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and pleaded with him, saying to him: "Lord, we wish to see Jesus."
Philip came and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
And Jesus answered them and said: "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Truly, truly I tell you: unless a grain of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it brings forth much fruit.
Whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world will inherit it in eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant will be also. If anyone serves me, my Father will honour him.
And now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour. But it was for this that I came to this hour.
Father, glorify your name!" A voice came from heaven: "I have glorified you, and I will glorify you again."
And the crowd that was standing there heard it and said: "It is thunder"; and others said: "An angel is speaking to him."
Jesus answered and said: "This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours.
Now is the judgment of the world; now the ruler of this world will be cast down.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all to myself."
He said this to signify by what death he was going to die.
The crowd answered him: "We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever. So how can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"

Jesus said to them: "The light is with you for only a little while longer. Walk while you still have the light with you, so that darkness may not overtake you; for whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
While the light is with you, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light." Jesus said this, and he went away and hid himself from them.
And although he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him,
so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he spoke: "Lord, who has believed what we have heard? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
For this reason they did not believe, because Isaiah also said:
"He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they may not see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them."
Isaiah said this because he saw his glory and spoke about him.
Yet even among the rulers many believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they would not declare it openly, so that they would not be expelled from the congregation.
For they loved human glory more than the glory of God.
And Jesus cried out and said: "Whoever believes in me does not believe in me, but in him who sent me.
And whoever sees me sees him who sent me.
I, the light of the world, have come, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness.
If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I do not judge him, for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
Whoever despises me and does not accept my words has one who judges him: the word that I spoke, that will judge him on the last day.
For I did not speak anything of myself; he commanded me what I should say and what I should speak.
And I know that his commandment is eternal life. That which [?] I [speak], as the Father commanded me, so I speak."
Before the feast of Passover, Jesus knew that his hour had come to depart from this world to the Father. Having loved his own who are in this world, he loved them completely.
And when it was the time of supper, the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon, the Iscariot, to betray him.
Jesus knew that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God.
He rose from the supper, laid aside his garment, took a towel, and girded himself.
And after that he took water, poured it into a basin, and began to wash the feet of the disciples and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.
He comes to Simon Peter, and Peter said to him: "Lord, are you washing my feet?"
Jesus answered him and said: "What I am doing you do not know now, but later you will know."
Peter said to him: "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered: "If I do not wash you, you will have no part with me."
Simon Peter said to him: "Lord, not only my feet, but my hands and my head too."
Jesus said to him: "Whoever has bathed has no need of washing, except only the washing of the feet, for he is completely clean. And you are clean, but not all of you."
For he knew who was going to betray him. That is why he said: "Not all of you are clean."
And when he had washed their feet, he took his garment and then reclined again [?]. And he said to them: "Do you know what I have done to you?
You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak rightly, for so I am.
If I, who am Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
For I have given you an example: as I have done to you, you also should do.
Truly, truly I say to you: a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is an apostle greater than the one who sent him.
If you know this, you will be blessed indeed, if you do it.
I am not speaking about all of you, for I know those whom I have chosen; but this is so that the scripture may be fulfilled: 'He who ate bread with me has carried out deceit against me.'
From now on I tell you, before it has happened, so that when it happens you may believe that I am he.
Truly, truly I tell you: whoever receives the one whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in his spirit, and he testified and said: Truly, truly I tell you that one of you will betray me.
His disciples looked at one another and were perplexed: about whom is he speaking?
And one of his disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at table beside Jesus.
Simon Peter beckoned to him to ask who it was that he was speaking about.
And he leaned back on Jesus' breast and said to him: Lord, who is it?
Jesus answered and said to him: It is the one to whom I will give the morsel after I have dipped it. And he dipped the morsel and gave it to Judas Iscariot.
And after that morsel, the devil entered then. And Jesus said to him: What you intend to do, do quickly!
And none of those reclining at table with him understood why he said this to him.
Some thought that, because Judas had the purse, Jesus had said to him: Buy what we need for this feast, or that he should give something to the poor.
And when he had taken that morsel, he went outside. And it was night.
And when he had gone out, Jesus said: Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.
And since God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him at once.
My children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will seek me, and as I said to the Jews, 'Where I am going, you cannot come,' so now I say to you.
I give you a new commandment, that you love one another: just as I have loved you, so you also are to love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.
Simon Peter said to him: Lord, where are you going? Jesus answered: Where I am going, you cannot follow me now, but later you will follow me.
Peter said to him: Lord, why can I not follow you? Even now I will lay down my life for you.
Jesus answered: Will you really lay down your life for me? Truly, truly I tell you: before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times.
Do not let your hearts be troubled; but believe in God, and believe in me.
In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. If it were not so, I would have told you: I am going to prepare a place for you.
And if I go, I will prepare a place for you, and then I will come and take you with me, so that where I am, there you may be also.
And you know where I am going, and you also know the way.
Thomas said to him: Lord, we do not know where you are going, so how can we know the way?
Jesus said to him: "I am the way and the truth and the life. No one can come to the Father except through me.
And if you had known me, you would have known my Father also. And from now on you know him and have seen him."
Philip said to him: "Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us."
Jesus said to him: "Have I been with you for so long a time, and you do not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. So how can you say, 'Show us the Father'?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak of myself; rather the Father, who dwells in me, he does the works.
Do you believe me that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? If not, then believe me because of those works.
Truly, truly I say to you: whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do, and he will do greater works than these, because I am going to the Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you love me, keep my commandments.
And I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Comforter, so that he may dwell with you forever:
that Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him and does not know him. But you know him, because he dwells with you and will be in you.
I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.
A little while longer, and this world will no longer see me, but you will see me; because I live, you too will live.
On that day you will know that I am in the Father, and you are in me, and I am in you.
Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will reveal myself to him."
Judas (not Iscariot) said to him: "Lord, how is it that you intend to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.
Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word that you hear is not mine, but the Father's who sent me.
I have told you these things while I am still with you.
But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have said to you.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not be afraid.
You heard me say to you, 'I am going away, and I am coming to you.' If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, for my Father is greater than I.
And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
I will not speak with you much longer, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he will find nothing in me.
But it is so that the world may know that I love the Father, and that I do just as the Father commanded me. Rise, let us go from here."
I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.
Every vine that abides in me and does not bear fruit, he will cut it off; and every one that bears fruit, he will cleanse it, and it will bear more fruit.
You are already clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.
Abide in me, and I in you. Just as a vine cannot bear fruit by itself unless it is firmly set on the root, so neither can you unless you are firmly set in me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. Whoever is firmly set in me, and I in him, he will bear much fruit, for without me you can do nothing.
If anyone does not abide in me, he is thrown out like a vine-branch and withers, and they gather it and throw it into the fire, and it is burned.
If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
By this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; remain firmly in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
I have told you this so that you may have my joy, and your joy may be made full.
This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
[?] No one has greater love than this, that he should lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, for the servant does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father I have told you.

It was not you who chose me, but I chose you and appointed you, so that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; and whatever you ask of my Father in my name, he will give you.
This I command you, that you love one another.
If the world hates you, know that it hated me first.
If you were of this world, this world would love its own; but because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.
Remember the word that I spoke to you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too; if they kept my word, they will keep yours too.
But they will do all this to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no guilt; but now they have no excuse for their sins.
Whoever hates me hates my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would have no guilt; but now they have seen and have hated both me and my Father.
But this is so that the word written in their law might be fulfilled: 'They hated me without cause.'
But when the Comforter comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me.
And you are witnesses, because you have been with me from the beginning.
I have told you this so that you will not stumble.
They will drive you out of their synagogues. Indeed, the hour will come when everyone who kills you will be counted as doing a service before God.
And they will do this to you because they have not known the Father, nor me.
But I have told you this too, so that when the hour comes you will remember that I told you. I did not tell you this from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, "Where are you going?"
But I have told you this, and sorrow has filled your hearts.
Yet I tell you the truth: it is better for you if I go away. If I do not go, the Comforter will not come to you; if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sins, concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment:
concerning sins, because they did not believe in me;
concerning righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you will no longer see me;
concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth, because he will not speak anything on his own, but he will speak whatever he hears, and he will tell you the things that are to come.
He will glorify me, because he will take from what is mine and tell it to you.
For everything that the Father has is mine. That is why I said to you that he will take from what is mine and tell it to you.
A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me, for I am going to my Father.
Some of his disciples said to one another, "What is this that he is telling us: 'A little while, and you will not see me; a little while longer, and you will see me'; and 'I am going to the Father'?"
And they said, "What is this 'little while'? We do not know what he is talking about."

Jesus knew that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, "Are you asking one another about this, that I said to you, 'A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me'?
Truly, truly I tell you: you will weep and lament, and the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

When a woman gives birth she has sorrow, because her hour has come. But when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the sorrow, because of her joy that a human being has been born into the world.
So you also are sorrowful now, but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
And on that day you will not ask me anything. Truly, truly I tell you: whatever you ask of my Father in my name, he will give you.
Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be full.
I have told you these things in parables. The hour will come when I will no longer speak to you in parables, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
I came out from the Father and came into the world; now I leave the world and go to the Father.
His disciples said to him: Look, now you are speaking plainly and are not speaking in any parable at all.
Now we know that you know all things, and there is no need for anyone to ask you anything. Because of this we believe that you came from God.
Jesus answered them and said: Do you believe now?
Look, the hours are coming, and have already come, when you will be scattered, each to his own place, and will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, for my Father is with me.
I have told you these things so that you may have peace with me. In this world you will be in distress, but take comfort, for I have overcome the world.
Jesus said these things, and he lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son also may glorify you,
just as you have given him authority over all flesh, so that he may give eternal life to all whom you have given him.
so that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent.
I have glorified you on earth. I have completed the work that you gave me to do.
And now, Father, glorify me with yourself, with the glory that I had from you before the creation of the world.
I have revealed your name to the people whom you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now they know that everything you have given me, I have given to them,
and they have truly accepted that I came from you, and they have believed that you sent me.
Now I pray to you for them. I do not pray for the world, but for these whom you have given me, for they are yours.
And all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I am glorified in them.
And I am no longer in the world, but these are in the world, and I am going to you. Holy Father, keep these in your name, by which you gave them to me, so that they may be one, just as we are one.
While I was in this world, I kept them in your name, by which you gave them to me. I kept them, and none of them was lost except the son of perdition, so that the scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am going to you, and I say this in this world so that they may have my joy in full within themselves.
I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of this world, just as I am not of the world.
But I do not ask you to take them out of the world. I ask that you keep them from the evil one.
They are not of this world, just as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them in the truth, for your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, so I too have sent them into the world.
And for their sake I sanctify myself, so that they too may be sanctified in the truth.
And I do not pray for these only, but for all who believe in me through their word,
so that all may be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you, so that they too may be in us, so that the world may also believe that you sent me.
And the glory which you gave me I will give to them, so that they may be one, as we are one:
I in them and you in me, so that they may be completely one, and the world may know that you sent me, and that I have loved them as you loved me.
Father, those whom you have given me, I desire that where I am they too may be with me, so that they may see my glory which you gave me, for you loved me before the creation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world did not know you, but I knew you, and these knew me, that you sent me.
And I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that [literally: because] the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I too in them.
When Jesus had said this, he went out with his disciples across the Kidron valley, where there was a garden, which he himself and his disciples entered.
Judas too, who was betraying him, knew that place, for Jesus had often gone there with his disciples.
And Judas took with him a band of soldiers and servants from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and came there with lamps and torches and swords.
But Jesus, when he saw all that was coming upon him, came out and said to them, "What are you seeking?"
They answered him, "Jesus the Nazarene." Jesus said to them, "I am he." Judas, who was betraying him, was standing with them too.
When he said to them, "I am he," they drew back and fell to the ground.
Then he asked them again, "Whom are you seeking?" And they said, "Jesus the Nazarene."
Jesus answered them, "I told you that I am he. If you are seeking me, let these men go."
This was so that the word he had spoken might be fulfilled: "Of those whom you gave me, I have lost not one."
Now Simon Peter, since he had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter, "Put that sword back into its sheath! The cup which you, Father, have given me, shall I not drink it?"
Then the band of soldiers and the commander and the servants of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him.
And they led him first to Annas, who was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
This was the Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter and the other disciple followed. And that disciple, because he was known to the high priest, went in with Jesus; he went into the courtyard of the high priest.
But Peter stood outside the gates. The other disciple, the one who was known to the high priest, came out, spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.
The maidservant who kept the door said to Peter, "Are you also one of that man's disciples?" And he said, "No."
The servants and slaves were standing there. They had lit a fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter also stood with them and warmed himself.
And the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Jesus answered him and said, "I spoke openly to the world. I always taught the people in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I said nothing in secret.
Why do you question me? Question those who heard what I said to them. Look, they know what I told them."
When he had said this to them, one of the servants standing there struck Jesus on the cheek and said, "Is that how you answer the high priest?"
And Jesus said to him, "If I said something evil, testify about the evil. But if it was good, why do you strike me?"
And Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
And Simon Peter was standing there warming himself. They said to him, "Are you also one of his disciples?" He denied it and said, "No."
And one of the high priest's slaves, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said to him, "Did I not see you in the garden with him?"
Peter denied it again. And at that very moment a cock crowed.
And they led Jesus from the house of Caiaphas to the judge's hall. It was just dawn. They themselves did not go into the hall, so that they would not be defiled but could eat the Passover.
So Pilate came out to them and said, "What evil deed do you charge this man with?"
They answered and said to him, "If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you."
