Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law." The Jews said to him, "It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death."
This was so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he had spoken to indicate by what death he was going to die.
Pilate went back into the hall, called Jesus, and said to him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus answered, "Do you say this of your own accord, or did others tell you about me?"
Pilate said, "Am I a Jew? Your own people and the high priests handed you over into my hands. What have you done?"

Jesus answered and said, "My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not of this world."

Pilate said to him, "If that is so, then you are a king?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice."
Pilate said to him, "What is truth?" And when he had said this, he went out again and said to the Jews, "I find no guilt at all in him.
But you have a custom that I release one man to you at this feast. Do you want me to release the king of the Jews to you?"
They all cried out, saying, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" And that Barabbas was a robber.
At that time Pilate took Jesus and scourged him.
And the soldiers made a crown of thorns and set it on his head, and they clothed him in purple.
And they would come before him and say to him, "Hail, King of the Jews!" And they struck him on the cheek.
Then Pilate went out again and said to them, "Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may understand that I find no guilt in him."
Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and dressed in the purple garment. Pilate said to them, "Here is the man!"
When the chief priests and the servants saw him, they cried out, saying, "Crucify, crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no guilt in him."
The Jews answered him, "We have a law, and according to our law he must die, because he made himself the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this word, he was more afraid.
He went back into the praetorium and said to Jesus, "Where are you from?" But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate said, "Will you not answer me? Do you not know that I have power to crucify you, and I have authority to release you?"
Jesus answered, "You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater guilt."
From then on Pilate wanted to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying, "If you release this man, you are not Caesar's friend. Everyone who declares himself a king is an opponent of Caesar."
When Pilate heard this word, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat, at the place called the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Kappatha.
It was the Preparation day (Friday) of the Passover, and it was about the sixth hour. And he said to the Jews, "Here is your king!"
And they cried out, "Take him away, take him away, and crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Shall I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered and said to him, "We have no king but Caesar."
Then he handed him over into their hands to be crucified. And they led him away.
And they led him, and he carried his own cross, and he went up to the place called the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgoltha.
There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on each side, and Jesus in the middle.
Pilate wrote on a board and put it on the cross. And it was written: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
Many of the Jews read that board, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. And it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, "Do not write, 'The King of the Jews,' but that he said, 'I am the King of the Jews.'"
Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."

When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and divided them into four parts, one part for each of the soldiers. But as for the tunic, since it was seamless, woven in one piece throughout from the top,

they said to one another, "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it to see whose it will be," so that the scripture might be fulfilled: "They divided my clothes among themselves, and for my tunic they cast lots." And the soldiers did this.
And standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, "Woman, behold, your son!"
And he said to the disciple, "Behold, your mother!" From that hour he took her into his own house.
After this Jesus saw that everything had been accomplished, and he said, "I thirst."
A vessel full of vinegar stood there. They filled a sponge with vinegar and gall, put it on a flower [?], and held it to his mouth.
When Jesus had received the vinegar with the gall, he said, "Everything has been accomplished." And he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

Since it was the day of Preparation, the Jews did not want the bodies to remain there on the Sabbath, because that Sabbath was a great day. So they asked Pilate to have their legs broken and the bodies taken away.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man, and likewise of the other who had been crucified with him.
But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.
But one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
The one who saw it has borne witness, and his testimony is true. He knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
This happened so that the scripture would be fulfilled: "Not a bone of his shall be broken."
And again another scripture says: "They shall look on him whom they pierced."
After this Joseph of Arimathea, who had been a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate to let him take down the body of Jesus, and Pilate gave the order.
Nicodemus also came, who had earlier come to Jesus by night, and he brought myrrh mixed with aloes, about a hundred pounds.
They took down the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, as was the custom of the Jews, and [?] for burial.
In the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
And because of the Preparation of the Jews, since the tomb was near, there they laid Jesus.
On the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came to the tomb early, at the first light of dawn, and saw the stone taken away from the door of the tomb.
Then she ran to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and said to them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him."
Peter and the other disciple went out and were going to the tomb.
The two of them were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and reached the tomb first.
He looked in and saw the linen cloths, but he did not go inside.
Simon Peter also came after him, went into the tomb, and saw the linen cloths lying there.
And the face-cloth that had been on his head was not lying with the other linen cloths, but was folded up by itself in one place.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also came in, and he saw and believed.
For he did not yet know the Scriptures, that he must rise from the dead.
Then the disciples gathered together again.
But Mary stood outside by the tomb, weeping. And as she wept, she looked down into the tomb,
and she saw two angels clothed in white, sitting one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been laid.
And they said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" She said to them, "Because they have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him."
And when she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?" She thought that he was the gardener, and she said to him, "Lord, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away."
Jesus said to her, "Mary!" And she turned and said to him in Hebrew, "Rabboni!", which is translated "Teacher."
Jesus said to her, "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and tell them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."
Mary Magdalene comes and brings the news to the disciples that she has seen the Lord, and that he said these things to her.

And in the evening of that day, the first day of the week, Jesus entered through the shut doors where the disciples had gathered for fear of the Jews. Jesus came, stood among them, and said to them, "Peace be with you!"
When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side, and the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
Then he said to them again, "Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, so I also send you."
And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit!
If you forgive anyone their sins, their sins are forgiven; and those whose sins you hold bound, let them be held bound."
But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called the Twin, was not with them when Jesus came.

The other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord." And he said to them, "Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, and put my finger into the place of the nails, and touch his side with my hand, I will not believe."
And after eight days his disciples gathered again, and Thomas was with them too. Jesus came in to them through the shut doors, stood among them, and said, "Peace be with you!"
Then he said to Thomas, "Bring your fingers and touch here, and see my hands; and bring your hand and put it into my side. Do not be unbelieving, but believe."
Thomas answered and said, "My Lord and my God!"
Jesus said to him, "Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen and have believed."
Jesus also did many other signs in front of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
But these were written so that you may believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and so that by believing you may receive eternal life in his name.
After this Jesus showed himself again to his disciples by the Sea of Tiberias, and he showed himself in this way:
Simon Peter was together with Thomas, who was called the Twin, and Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of his disciples.
Simon Peter said to them, "I am going fishing." They said to him, "We will go with you too." They went out and got into the boat. That night they caught nothing at all.
When morning came, Jesus was standing on the seashore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
Jesus said to them, "Children, do you have anything to eat?" They answered him, "No."
He said to them, "Cast that net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some." They cast it, and they could not haul it in because of the great number of fish.

The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord." When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he wrapped his outer garment around himself, because he was naked, and threw himself into the sea.
The other disciples came in the boat, because they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits away, and they dragged the net with the fish.
When they came out onto land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, with a fish on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish that you have just caught."
Simon Peter went in and hauled the net onto land, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three of them. Though it was full with so many, the net was not torn.
Jesus said, "Come and have breakfast." None of the disciples dared to ask him, "Who are you?" They knew that it was the Lord.
Jesus took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish likewise.
This was the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after he had risen from the dead.
When they had had breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?" He said, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." He said to him, "Feed my lambs."
Then he said to him again, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?" He said to him, "Yes, Lord, for I love you." He said to him, "Tend my sheep."

He said to him the third time, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?" Peter was grieved because he had said to him the third time, "Do you love me?" He said to him, "Lord, you know all things, and you perceive all things, and that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Feed my sheep.

Truly, truly, I say to you: when you were young, you fastened your own belt and went wherever you wished. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and others will fasten your belt and lead you where you do not want to go."
He said this to indicate by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. After he had said this, he said to him, "Follow me!"
Peter turned around and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them, the one who had leaned on his breast and asked, "Lord, who is the one who will betray you?"
When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, "Lord, what about him?"
Jesus said to him, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me."
So the saying spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die. But Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but rather, "If I want him to remain until I come."
This is the disciple who testifies about these things and who wrote them down, and you know that his testimony is true.
But there are also many other things that Jesus did. If each one of them were written down, this world could not hold the books that would be written.
